newsitem.title: UK: WEEK AHEAD-UK gilts to consolidate, all eyes on RPI.
newsitem.headline: WEEK AHEAD-UK gilts to consolidate, all eyes on RPI.

text.p: UK gilts are set to consolidate after last week's dramatic rally with all eyes on Thursday's retail prices data for the latest information on price pressures building in the economy, analysts said on Monday.
"After the rally we saw last week things will probably slow down," said Phil Tyson, senior international economist at HSBC.
The short end of the market should remain positive, but it could take a knock from a firm RPI number, analysts said.

And most agreed the scope for further gains in ultra long gilts was limited. That part of the curve outperformed last week as the market grew more optimistic about the outlook for inflation long term after finance minister Gordon Brown granted the Bank of England operational independence.
Tyson tipped the five-year area as holding most value short-term. The outperformance of longer-dated gilts has left five year paper looking attractive, he said.
"In the next week we think five years are pretty good value and we're advising people to move in there. They are traditionally good value just before an auction."
The Bank of England is set to tap the five year area on May 20 and will give details of the amount on Tuesday at 1430 GMT.
For the short end of the market, the RPI data will be a key focus.

Comments from Bank of England Governor Eddie George on Monday that the UK's chances of hitting the official inflation target of 2.5 percent have improved to better than even may have primed the market to make a move.
Gilts will get a more definitive insight into his views when the Bank publishes its quarterly inflation report on Tuesday at 1030 GMT.
But the official inflation data will be crucial for gilts.
"If we get any softer data, there might be a temptation for gilts to get over bullish, although there's been no great reaction to the PPI," said Mark Miller, UK economist at Morgan Stanley.
Producer prices data on Monday showed UK output prices rose 0.2 percent in April for a year-on-year inflation rate of just 0.8 percent. Input prices fell 1.9 percent on the month.
A Reuters consensus poll of analysts forecast a 0.6 percent rise in April allowing the year-on-year rate to drop to 2.5 percent from 2.6 percent in March.
Underlying inflation is forecast to edge lower in April, to 2.6 percent from 2.7 percent in March.

"The data are not looking particularly negative but not good enough to spark a move. We are expecting some profit taking but the mood remaining good," said Tom Rayner, international economist at Societe Generale.
He expected a small recovery in food prices could push the RPI figure higher.

And gilts will have the latest look at inflationary pressures in the labour market when official unemployment figures are released on Wednesday. Average earnings are forecast to stay steady at 5.0 percent in March with unemployment expected to fall by 40,000 in April.
Analysts said the gilt/Bund spread was set to narrow during the week, aided by the improved inflationary outlook.
"The gilt/Bund spread could come into 130 to 135 basis points this week," said Rayner.
The spread widened to 138 basis points on Monday from 134 on Friday.
